title: Not every timezone is a whole number of hours from UTC -- Nepal is 5 hours and 45 minutes off
assumption: A UTC offset is always a whole number of hours (or at worst, whole 30-minute steps).

input.description: Scheduling a meeting, computing 'business hours', or bucketing timestamps by local hour for users in Nepal, India, or several Pacific/Indian Ocean zones.

what_goes_wrong: Code that converts an offset to hours with integer math (`offset_minutes // 60`) or assumes `local_hour = (utc_hour + offset_hours) % 24` is correct silently produces times that are off by 15, 30, or 45 minutes for users in these zones.
why: UTC offsets are defined per timezone by the IANA tz database and are not required to be whole hours. Nepal Standard Time is UTC+05:45, India Standard Time is UTC+05:30, and historically several zones have used offsets like +04:51 or +08:05:43 before standardization. Any code path that models 'timezone' as 'an integer number of hours' or truncates a fractional offset will misplace every timestamp converted through it by the truncated remainder.

repros.code:
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo
from datetime import datetime

kathmandu = datetime(2024, 6, 1, 12, 0, tzinfo=ZoneInfo("Asia/Kathmandu"))
kolkata = datetime(2024, 6, 1, 12, 0, tzinfo=ZoneInfo("Asia/Kolkata"))
print("Kathmandu offset:", kathmandu.utcoffset())
print("Kolkata offset:", kolkata.utcoffset())
print("naive hour-only offset would truncate to:", kathmandu.utcoffset().seconds // 3600, "hours, losing the 45 minutes")
repros.expected_output:
Kathmandu offset: 5:45:00
Kolkata offset: 5:30:00
naive hour-only offset would truncate to: 5 hours, losing the 45 minutes

Kathmandu offset minutes: 345
Kolkata offset minutes: 330

fix: Always carry UTC offsets (and do timezone conversion) in minutes or seconds, never truncated hours, and let the timezone library (zoneinfo, Intl) compute the offset rather than hand-rolling it from a hours table.
